sections.prompt: [curious] Why do your fingers go wrinkly in the bath? [excited] Most people think water soaks into your skin. [deadpan] Nope. [mischievously] It's your nervous system. [curious] After about five minutes in water, your nerves tell the blood vessels in your fingertips to shrink. Less volume underneath... so the skin folds up. [excited] Doctors even noticed that fingers with damaged nerves don't wrinkle at all! [curious] So why would your body do this on purpose? [whispers] Grip. [excited] In one experiment, people with wrinkly fingers moved wet marbles faster. The wrinkles channel water away, like the treads on a tire. [confidently] So pruney fingers... are your body's built-in rain tires.
